title: Helmsman Onboarding Activation Briefing
summary: Kickoff for Helmsman's onboarding to Redwood Inference. Covered deployment options (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), security controls (SSO, KMS, audit logs), performance expectations, and initial runbook and timeline for pilot. Agreed next steps: security questionnaire, pilot scope doc, and a 2-week performance benchmark run. Action owners assigned.
topics: Deployment options and network topology (VPC vs on-prem)
Security and compliance: SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
Performance expectations: p99 latency, throughput, batching
action_items: Arjun: share sample inference traffic profile (qps, avg seq len) by 2027-02-03
Marcus: deliver proposed pilot config and cost estimate (Dedicated vs Private) by 2027-02-01
Maya: upload completed security questionnaire to the shared drive by 2027-02-05
Priya: schedule pilot kickoff and create runbook draft by 2027-02-02
next_steps: SE to provision pilot cluster (staging) and send access details: https://redwood.example/pilot/helmsman
Customer to provide sample logs and a small prompt set for quality checks
Security team to review Redwood SOC2 + KMS docs attached in the follow-up email
Schedule a 30-min perf sync after 7 days of pilot data
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Lena, Marcus, Priya (Redwood); Arjun, Sophie, Diego, Maya (Helmsman)

00:00 Lena Ortega: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick intros and then dive into the onboarding plan, is that okay?
00:12 Arjun Rao: yeah sounds good, thanks Lena. Arjun here, head of ML at Helmsman. quick note our main constraint is latency for customer-facing summarization, target p99 under 350ms for 1k tokens.
00:26 Marcus Chen: okay got it, that's helpful, and do you have a qps expectation?
00:30 Arjun Rao: we expect bursts up to 80 qps and steady ~15 qps, average seq length 280 tokens, sometimes 1k in batch jobs.
00:40 Sophie Meyers: and from infra side we prefer VPC peering for initial pilot, we are open to on-prem later.
00:47 Lena Ortega: perfect. quick agenda, we'll cover deployment choices, security, perf expectations and then pilot scope. Marcus will lead the technical bits.
01:00 Marcus Chen: cool. so deployment: three options we discussed earlier — hosted API (fastest), dedicated reserved capacity, or Redwood Private deployed in your VPC / on-prem. for your latency numbers, Dedicated in AWS region close to your users or Private w/ VPC peering will give the lowest network tail.
01:22 Diego Alvarez: can you remind us what the difference is in terms of data egress and logs between Dedicated and Private?
01:28 Marcus Chen: yes — Dedicated keeps compute in Redwood-managed infra but data is isolated at tenant level, logs and audit are available in the Console; Private gives you control — customer-managed networking and optional on-prem so logs and storage sit in your account. egress costs depend on your cloud config, but Private removes cross-account egress.
01:48 Maya Lin: on encryption — we need KMS/HSM integration and proof traffic doesn't hit a public tier. how do you manage keys?
01:56 Marcus Chen: we support BYOK with AWS KMS and HSM integrations. for the control plane, we can use customer-managed KMS keys for at-rest encryption. we'll share the KMS integration guide.
02:08 Sophie Meyers: and SSO? we have SAML 2.0 with Okta.
02:13 Priya Patel: Redwood supports SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning and fine-grained RBAC. we'll send the SSO runbook after the call.
02:21 Arjun Rao: do you have SOC2 cert?
02:24 Lena Ortega: yes, SOC 2 Type II. we'll attach latest attestation and the security whitepaper.
02:31 Marcus Chen: turning to perf. for 280 token avg and p99 350ms, the levers are model choice (smaller opt quantized variants), batching, and KV prefix caching. often the biggest wins are batching and prefix caching for repeated system prompts. also model selection — Redwood offers a catalog of curated models with perf profiles in Console.
02:57 Diego Alvarez: how aggressive is the quantization impact on quality? we can't drop below a certain rouge for our summarization.
03:03 Marcus Chen: right it's a tradeoff. we can run a quality regression with your prompt set. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles by workload; typically int8 gives big perf gains with small quality delta but we should verify with your evals.
03:18 Arjun Rao: great, we'll provide a small eval set.
03:21 Marcus Chen: ideal. pilot plan suggestion: 2-week staging run — week 1 smoke tests and correctness checks against your prompt set; week 2 perf run at scaled QPS to observe caching and batching effects. we'll mirror production traffic patterns you send.
03:37 Sophie Meyers: what about canary rollouts and fallbacks? if model fails we need automatic fallbacks.
03:42 Marcus Chen: Console supports rollout policies and automatic fallback to an agreed model variant or hosted fallback. we can configure canary percents and automatic rollback on error thresholds.
03:51 Maya Lin: on audit logs — do you provide token-level logs or just request metadata? we have strict data retention rules.
03:57 Marcus Chen: we can log request metadata and offer redaction options; for token-level logging that's optional and controlled by you. for Private, logs can remain in your account.
04:08 Lena Ortega: okay quick recap on responsibilities: Helmsman provides traffic profile, prompt set, and security questionnaire. Redwood provides pilot infra, pilot config, and runbook draft. Priya will coordinate.
04:20 Priya Patel: I'll set up the workspace and a runbook template in Confluence and share links by tomorrow.
04:25 Arjun Rao: timeline — how quickly can we start?
04:28 Marcus Chen: we can start provisioning staging in 3 business days after we get sample traffic and a programmatic service account for access; actual pilot start depends on SSO and network setup.
04:40 Diego Alvarez: quick network question: do you prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink?
04:44 Marcus Chen: peering is simpler for most customers; PrivateLink is possible if you need extra control. we'll include both network diagrams in the follow-up.
04:55 Sophie Meyers: cost — rough order of magnitude for Dedicated reserved vs Private?
04:59 Lena Ortega: we'll put together a ballpark estimate. Marcus can include expected units for the pilot config and a monthly delta for Dedicated vs Private.
05:10 Marcus Chen: yes I'll include run-rate and pilot cost; note that batching and KV cache efficiency can materially lower per-token cost during steady state.
05:20 Arjun Rao: any friction on deploying our models? we use standard transformer weights but with some custom ops.
05:25 Marcus Chen: our runtime handles common ops and we have a model-onboarding checklist. for uncommon ops we may need a short compatibility shim — we'll flag that in the pilot config.
05:35 Maya Lin: compliance question: we need an auditor to validate controls. will Redwood sign an ATO package?
05:42 Lena Ortega: we have a standard ATO playbook and can support auditor requests; we'll coordinate with our security team and share the package.
05:50 Sophie Meyers: great. any performance showstoppers we should be aware of?
05:53 Marcus Chen: sometimes network tail and cold KV caches cause spikes. that's why we recommend warming and a short canary to measure p95/p99 before full rollout.
06:03 Arjun Rao: ok. let's talk about concrete next steps.
06:06 Priya Patel: action items: Marcus will send pilot config and estimate; Arjun will send traffic profile; Maya will complete security questionnaire. I'll publish runbook draft and schedule the kickoff meeting.
06:18 Sophie Meyers: can you share sample dashboards? we'd like to see token-level cost, per-route latency.
06:23 Marcus Chen: yes Console has those; I'll attach a read-only sample dashboard link.
06:28 Diego Alvarez: also need alerting hooks to our pager system.
06:31 Marcus Chen: we integrate with PagerDuty and Slack and can ship webhooks for tracing.
06:36 Arjun Rao: any recommended quantization levels to start with?
06:39 Marcus Chen: start with int8 for perf eval; if quality is impacted, we can test mixed precision and int8-web options. Redwood Optimize will provide suggestions based on eval results.
06:48 Lena Ortega: closing — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with email and links. 
06:53 Sophie Meyers: thanks, appreciate it.
06:56 Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: some proper nouns garbled (e.g., PrivateLink sometimes transcribed as "private link"), occasional filler words and interruptions, timestamps approximate.
